discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

motivation: For three decades gamma-ray bursts, the most luminous explosions known, had no known distance or physical origin. In 1997 Costa and Frontera used the BeppoSAX Wide Field Cameras and Narrow Field Instruments to make rapid, arcminute X-ray localizations, which led to the discovery of fading X-ray afterglows. Using these positions, Kulkarni and collaborators found radio and optical counterparts and measured redshifts that placed the bursts at cosmological distances. This proved that the bursts release energies comparable to a stellar rest mass in relativistic, collimated jets. Their work turned an unexplained phenomenon into a precise probe of black-hole formation, the deaths of massive stars and the high-redshift universe. It also set up the multi-wavelength, rapid-response approach to transients that underpins time-domain and multi-messenger astronomy, including the GW170817 kilonova. Instrumental daring and the immediate physical insight it produced are the hallmarks of this achievement.
